# Results — Study 174 (Bitcoin-Rainbow) on real BTC-USD daily tape

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim: buying in the
"cold" coloured bands of the Bitcoin Rainbow Chart (low σ deviations from the log-time
regression) and selling in the "hot" bands earns superior risk-adjusted returns. We
replicate the in-sample result, then expose it as a pure look-ahead artefact by
re-fitting on a walk-forward (expanding window) basis. As-of **2026-06-15**; full history
from Yahoo Finance.*

## Data stamp

| Ticker | Window | N rows | Fingerprint |
|---|---|--:|---|
| BTC-USD | 2014-09-17 -> 2026-06-12 | 4,287 | `902481b7aa10` |

Log-time regressor is computed deterministically from the BTC genesis block date
(2009-01-03); no price data is needed to construct it.

## The Rainbow Chart — what it is

The Bitcoin Rainbow Chart (popularised by Blockchaincenter.net, 2014) fits:

    log(price) = alpha + beta * log(days since 2009-01-03) + epsilon

using the *entire* available history and places 9 coloured bands at ±k*sigma_resid
offsets (k = 1, 2, 3, 4) from the regression line. The label "Fire sale" sits at
< -4σ; "Maximum bubble territory" sits at > +4σ. The recipe: buy when price is in
the cold bands, sell when it is in the hot bands.

## In-sample (look-ahead-biased) result

Fitting the regression on the whole history (2014-2026) and then back-applying it to
the same history produces impressive-looking metrics:

| Metric | Value |
|---|--:|
| **Signal threshold** | buy < -1σ, sell > +1.5σ |
| **Annualised return** | **+20.7%** |
| **Annualised Sharpe** | **+1.16** |
| **HAC t-stat (mean daily return)** | **+4.53** |
| Time in market | 15.3% |
| Buy-and-hold ann. return | +33.7% |

A t-stat of +4.53 would, in most contexts, be compelling evidence of a real edge.
**Here it is entirely an artefact**: the 2013 "buy" signals were generated knowing that
BTC would reach $69,000 in 2021. Strip out that future information and the result changes
completely.

## Walk-forward (honest) result — the look-ahead bonus evaporates

Expanding-window re-fit: at each date *t*, only data through *t* is used to estimate
the regression parameters. Signal at *t* → position entered at *t+1*.

| Metric | Value |
|---|--:|
| **Signal threshold** | buy < -1σ, sell > +1.5σ |
| **Annualised return** | **+2.2%** |
| **Annualised Sharpe** | **+0.09** |
| **HAC t-stat (mean daily return)** | **+0.39** |
| Time in market | 19.2% |
| Buy-and-hold ann. return | +33.7% |
| **Delta t (IS minus WF)** | **+4.14** |

The HAC t-stat drops from +4.53 to +0.39 — solidly inside the noise band. The strategy
earns +2.2%/yr while a simple buy-and-hold on BTC earns +33.7%/yr. The walk-forward
strategy spends 80% of its time flat and misses the bulk of Bitcoin's historic rise.

## Could you trade it? — cost sweep (walk-forward)

| Round-trip cost | Annualised return | HAC t-stat |
|---|--:|--:|
| 0 bps (gross) | +2.2% | +0.39 |
| 10 bps | +2.0% | +0.36 |
| 50 bps | +1.4% | +0.25 |
| 100 bps | +0.6% | +0.11 |

At any realistic cost level the walk-forward strategy is an inferior substitute for
holding BTC. The t-stat never clears 2, even at zero cost.

## The look-ahead anatomy

| Phase | Bands "know" about | Result |
|---|---|---|
| IS fit (2014 era) | 2015–2026 prices | Beautifully prescient "sell" signal near $69k ATH |
| WF fit (2014 era) | Only 2014 data | Bands are wildly uncertain; most signals never fire |
| WF fit (2021 era) | 2014–2021 data | Bands finally reasonable; signal mostly gone |

The rainbow chart's entire visual appeal comes from fitting a line through 12+ years of
BTC history and then *pretending* that the bands were known at the left edge of the chart.

## Band sigma distribution

| Statistic | In-sample | Walk-forward |
|---|--:|--:|
| Mean | 0.000 | +0.09 |
| Std | 1.00 | 1.22 |
| Min | −1.51 | −2.16 |
| Max | +3.65 | +3.97 |

In-sample: the regression is fitted on the full history so residuals are mean-zero by
construction and std = 1.00 exactly. Walk-forward: the regression is still catching up
in the early years (high estimation uncertainty), hence wider distribution.

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** Walk-forward HAC t-stat = +0.39 (well below the |t| = 2 bar).
  The impressive in-sample t = +4.53 is entirely a look-ahead artefact (delta-t = +4.14).
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** Walk-forward strategy earns +2.2%/yr vs buy-and-hold +33.7%/yr.
  The rainbow keeps the investor in cash 80% of the time, missing the asset's primary trend.
  At any cost level the signal t-stat does not clear 2.
- **Overfitting exposed — BUSTED.** The rainbow chart is a log-time regression fitted on the
  entire available history: it always looks perfect in-sample and always fails out of sample.
  The bands are not discovered; they are constructed to contain past prices.
